messages.subject: Different results in PCA
parts:
Dear everyone, I just started working with GM, and due to my initial lack of confidence in conducting analyses, I opted to run them using different software to validate the results.

Initially, I measured my meshes using Meshlab and Slicer to ensure the accuracy of my scale. The dimensions of the individuals in both software programs closely matched those obtained with a caliper, affirming the correctness of the scale.

Subsequently, I utilized Checkpoint (Stratovan) to pplace my landmarks and exported the coordinates of my specimens at their original scale. This software suppose to export coordinates with the scale already incorporated, as indicated by the company's support team. However, upon conducting the Generalized Procrustes Analysis and PCA in two different softwares, MorphoJ and R (geomorph package), I encountered starkly divergent results.

Could anyone offer insight into what might be causing this disparity? I thank you all in advance, Best regards, Bruno

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Different results in PCA
parts:
Bruno,

 

Your email is unclear as to what precisely was different. Did you use different landmarking schemes in each analytical package for the PCA? Was it the same data in both packages for the PCA?  At what stage, and in what software, was GPA performed?

 

There are numerous reasons things can differ between MorphoJ and geomorph. Some of these have been mentioned in prior posts (MorphoJ uses full Procrustes fitting, it does not perform sliding of semilandmarks, etc.).


Dean
